note: Evidence-access audit updated 2026-10-29. Full AAD page content was available for the acne treatment, pregnancy acne treatment, retinoid/retinol, patch-testing, and sunscreen guidance pages during this audit. Other sources may still be represented only by search excerpts or abstracts; check each source before relying on a specific claim. Secondary sources are context only and should not be sole support for a safety restriction.

tiers.institutional: University, hospital system, or clinical education site
tiers.secondary: Journalism or commercial health content quoting clinicians; context only, never sole support for a safety rule

sources.title: Acne: Diagnosis and treatment
sources.supports: AAD says treatment plans may combine topical therapies and lists prescribed retinoid + benzoyl peroxide combinations including Epiduo, Epiduo Forte and Twyneo; it advises following dermatologist instructions.

sources.title: Acne Vulgaris: Treatment Guidelines from the AAD
sources.supports: Benzoyl peroxide plus a topical retinoid is a first-line combination for acne, so the pair is not inherently contraindicated.

sources.title: Retinoid or retinol?
sources.supports: Retinol is an OTC retinoid; the page advises using the lowest-intensity formula and says retinoids should not be used during pregnancy. It recommends dermatologist advice and sun protection.

sources.title: Sunscreen FAQs
sources.supports: Use broad-spectrum, SPF 30 or higher, water-resistant sunscreen; reapply approximately every two hours when outdoors and after swimming or sweating; no sunscreen is waterproof.

sources.title: How to test skin care products
sources.organization: American Academy of Dermatology (press release via Newswise)
sources.supports: Apply a product to a small test spot twice daily for 7–10 days, following normal use directions; stop if a reaction occurs. This does not guarantee facial tolerance.

sources.title: Topical therapy for acne
sources.supports: Combining acne agents (for example with benzoyl peroxide or a topical retinoid) may result in a cumulative irritant effect.

sources.title: Acne handout (University Student Health Services)
sources.supports: If advised to use both benzoyl peroxide and a topical retinoid, use benzoyl peroxide in the morning and the retinoid at bedtime; benzoyl peroxide increases oxidation of the retinoid medication.

sources.title: Case-based experience with simultaneous use of a fixed topical antibiotic/benzoyl peroxide combination and a topical retinoid
sources.supports: Abstract discusses simultaneous use of newer-generation retinoids and benzoyl peroxide products without concern of retinoid degradation. Only the abstract excerpt was seen.

sources.title: Is retinol safe during pregnancy?
sources.supports: Safest approach is to avoid topical retinoids during pregnancy and breastfeeding; OTC retinol is lower in active vitamin A than prescription retinoids but evidence is limited; oral retinoids must never be used in pregnancy.

sources.title: Acne and retinoid guidance
sources.organization: Ro (telehealth content citing AAD and Zaenglein 2016)
sources.supports: Retinoids cause dryness, peeling, redness; reduce frequency to limit effects; avoid other topical acne treatments containing sulfur, resorcinol or salicylic acid while using retinoids; many prescribers do not recommend retinoids in pregnancy.

sources.title: Good News: It's Safe AND Effective to Use Niacinamide and Vitamin C Together
sources.supports: Dermatologists quoted say the idea that vitamin C and niacinamide do not mix is a myth.

sources.title: Niacinamide and vitamin C
sources.supports: Products containing vitamin C can be used with products containing niacinamide; older avoid-together guidance is described as outdated.

sources.title: The Right Way to Use Benzoyl Peroxide and Retinol Together
sources.supports: Quoted dermatologists say benzoyl peroxide can oxidise retinol and reduce its effectiveness, mixing can irritate, and both can be used if the approach is intentional.

sources.title: Ingredients you should not use together
sources.supports: One dermatologist advises caution stacking retinol with AHAs/BHAs (dryness). The same article's pH claim about vitamin C and retinol is a single unreferenced assertion and is NOT relied on.

sources.title: Is any acne treatment safe to use during pregnancy?
sources.supports: AAD says tazarotene should not be used during pregnancy and most experts recommend stopping adapalene and tretinoin; it advises consultation with an obstetrician or dermatologist before acne treatment during pregnancy.
